In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more robust and economical method for phylogenetic analysis of closely related bacteria and with the identification of the best genes for this purpose.
the development of a more accurate and efficient method to assess intraspecies diversity.
the development of a robust and cost-effective approach to the study of intraspecies diversity, using the fewest possible genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a small number of genes that have been shown to perform well for the phylogenetic study of closely related organisms is likely to be more accurate and more cost-effective than the use of a large number of genes that are not necessarily well suited to the task.

a few best-performing genes, as defined here, can be used as an effective proxy for the whole-genome-based assessment of intraspecies diversity, and the use of multiple genes is not always better than that of a few best-performer genes.
the phylogenetic accuracy of closely related organisms can be significantly improved by selecting a few best-performing genes for phylogenetic studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to achieve a more accurate and robust phylogeny, one can use fewer genetic markers, provided that they are carefully selected.

, to achieve the most cost-effective phylogeny of closely related bacteria, the selection of a few genes should be guided by the whole-genome-level ANI and the robustness of each gene in the genome to phylogenetic reconstruction.

the phylogeny of closely related organisms is robust and that the selection of the most phylogenetically informative genes is critical for accurate phylogenetic reconstruction at the intraspecies and even interstrain levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single best gene for phylogenetic analysis is not necessarily available, and a combination of several genes that are robust to intraspecies variation is needed.

phylogenetic analysis at the intraspecies and interspecies levels should be based on the average ANI of a small number of carefully selected genes rather than the concatenated alignment of many genes.
the phylogenetic analysis of closely related organisms can be performed more efficiently and accurately using just a few genes that are best suited for the purpose.
